filo export retention [DIR] -o FILE
filo export duplicates [DIR] -o FILE

  Writes every file under DIR (inside a root), or under every root, as CSV
  (UTF-8) to FILE, which must not exist. Columns: id, export, directory, name,
  size, modified, file_date, retention, keep_until. Fill in retention in a
  spreadsheet, then run filo update FILE. A blank file_date is filled in from
  the file name when the name holds one clear date (2023-03-14, 20230314, or
  2023-03 for the month's last day); check it. On a large system, export one
  directory at a time.

  export duplicates writes each duplicate group (two or more copies of the same
  content; hard links to one file are one copy) with a copy under DIR, with all
  its copies. Columns: id, export, group, copies, directory, name, size,
  modified, file_date, retention, keep_until, action. In each group you decide
  on, write keep for the copy to keep and delete for the rest (or k and d); keep
  on two or more copies makes them records, each kept with its own retention;
  always on every row means the content belongs everywhere. A group left blank
  is left alone. filo delete FILE carries the CSV out.

Flags
  -o FILE                  the CSV to write; it must not exist
